result.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
result.summary: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EATS on tool-augmented medical reasoning tasks, including closed-ended visual question answering and free-form report generation. Experiments on four public datasets, ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA, across three multimodal LLMs, Qwen3-VL 2B, Qwen3-VL 32B, and GPT-5.5, show consistent gains in tool selection behavior and downstream medical reasoning performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Limingyuan001/EATS.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EATS：将历史工具调用轨迹（查询、所选工具、参数与自评反馈）构建为可检索经验记忆，用其引导医疗多模态推理代理在新查询上的工具选择；在 ChestAgentBench、CheXbench、MIMIC-CXR、SLAKE-VQA 及三个多模态模型上验证工具选择行为与下游任务表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无需真值监督、随测试时经验扩展」的轨迹记忆可用于核查 LVR 中「LOOK」式的证据获取与工具/证据筛选策略，以及自评反馈在贡献分配与停止决策上的作用；但论文聚焦外部工具选择而非内部 latent 推理状态，联系需进一步核实。
